AgentHandoffParams.description:
Hands the session of the agent in `pane_id` over to another agent: a new
tab after the source tab, in the source pane's directory, starts `to` with
a first prompt that points at the source session's transcript. The source
tab stays as it is.

to.description: The agent to continue the work: `claude`, `pi` or `codex`.

AgentLimitKind.description: Which limit ended an agent's turn; the remedies differ.

oneOf.description: A usage or rate limit that resets on its own.
Out of credits or a billing problem: waiting does not help.

AgentPromptConfirmedParams.description:
Types a prompt like `agent.prompt` and answers only once the agent shows it accepted it: the
turn report of the prompt (Claude's `UserPromptSubmit`, Pi's turn start) for an agent that
reports turns, else the agent's state turning `working`. An agent already `working` when the
prompt is typed has its input open and queues it, so the written submission is the
acknowledgement. A dialog (`blocked`) or an agent not ready is refused before typing, naming
the dialog when screen detection recognizes it; a dialog that appears after typing, before
the acknowledgement, answers `agent_prompt_blocked` without typing again. It has no timeout:
it waits for one of these events, the agent's exit, or the caller closing the connection.

AgentPromptTrackedParams.description:
Types a prompt like `agent.prompt` and returns at once with the request herdr follows
(`prompt_request`), for `agent.wait_turn`. Refused with `turn_tracking_unsupported`, before
anything is typed, when the agent does not report its turns.

AgentPromptTurnParams.description:
Sends a prompt like `agent.prompt` and waits until the turn that prompt started ends, as the
agent's integration reports it. Refused with `turn_tracking_unsupported`, before anything is
typed, when the agent does not report its turns.

AgentPromptWaitOptions.description:
Makes `agent.prompt` wait after typing. From a non-working state it first waits for the
agent's acknowledgement, the same as `agent.prompt_confirmed` (the prompt's turn report, else
the agent turning `working`), with no time limit of its own; then it waits for one of `until`
(default `idle`, `done` or `blocked`). A dialog before the acknowledgement answers with the
`blocked` agent when `until` includes `blocked`, else `agent_prompt_blocked` naming the
dialog. `timeout_ms` is the caller's: when it passes before the acknowledgement the answer is
`agent_prompt_stalled`, after it `timeout`.

timeout_ms.description: Startup timeout in milliseconds. Values must be greater than 3000 and at most 300000.

AgentWaitTurnParams.description:
Waits until the turn a followed prompt (`agent.prompt_tracked`, `agent.prompt`) started
ends, and says how it ended. It checks the request and subscribes to its changes in one
step, so a turn that ended before the wait began still answers `finished`. It has no
timeout: every outcome is an event, and a request herdr no longer knows (its server
restarted) answers `unknown_request` at once.

ClientShellSurfaceSetParams.description: Updates whether the requesting client shell receives and controls pane presentation.

command_id.description: Opaque endpoint-issued command identifier from the client-shell projection.

selection.description: Client-owned selection coordinates, validated against the pane's content revision.

pane_id.description: The coordinator's pane (the CLI sends its `HERDR_PANE_ID`).

repo.description:

NotificationShowForPaneParams.description:
`notification.show` about a pane: clicking the desktop notification focuses
that pane's tab, or its workspace once the tab is gone. A separate method
rather than an optional field, so an older server rejects it instead of
showing a notification that silently ignores the target.

PaneClearAwaitingReplyParams.description:
The user dismisses the agents' questions in these panes without typing into them: their
awaiting-reply reports are forgotten as if the user had typed. A later report shows the
question again.

PaneForgetAgentSessionParams.description:
The user ended this agent session (for example with `/exit`), so a restart
must not resume it. Only the matching session is forgotten, and a report
older than the pane's latest session report is ignored.

resume_argv.description:
Command that resumes this agent's session after a Herdr restart. The
first element must be a plain command name.

Command that resumes this agent's session after a Herdr restart. The
first element must be a plain command name.

turn_reports.description: The integration reports this agent's turns with `pane.report_turn`.

PaneReportAgentStoppedParams.description:
The OS stopped this agent session (Claude reports a `SessionEnd` with
reason `other`, for example after a signal). Once its process has left the
pane, Herdr resumes the session there. Ignored unless the session runs in
or just exited the pane.

PaneReportAwaitingReplyParams.description:
The agent in the pane ends its current turn by asking the user something: a question or a
decision the user must make. Shown until the agent starts working again.

question.description:
The question in a few words (`Install now?`), shown under the agent in the list of
agents waiting on the user. Cut to about 40 characters on a character boundary, control
characters dropped; without it the list shows only that the agent waits for a reply.

PaneReportLimitParams.description:
The agent's turn ended on a limit (a usage limit, out of credits) and it waits until the
user acts or the limit resets. Shown, with the reset time when herdr knows it, until the
user types into the pane or dismisses it, like an awaiting-reply report.

message.description: The agent's own error text; cut to one short line.

PaneReportTaskParams.description:
The agent in the pane names the task it works on now, in a few words; `None` or an empty
text forgets it. Shown as the tab's name, ahead of the terminal title (which agents set once
per session), until the agent reports another one, exits or changes session.

PaneReportTurnParams.description:
The agent's integration reports that a turn started (with the prompt that started it) or
ended. Herdr follows the prompts it typed (`agent.prompt`) through these reports only.

continuation.description:
With `started`: the turn continues the running prompt's work (a background task's
notification) instead of starting a new prompt, so it ends no prompt's turn.

error.description:
With `finished`: the turn ended on this error (Claude's `StopFailure`), so the prompts
it ran end as failed.

interrupted.description: With `finished`: the turn was interrupted, so the prompts it ran end as interrupted.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

force.description:
Hand off even while headless worker processes are alive; they get
SIGTERM and end with this server. Worker pipes are not handed over,
so without this any live worker refuses the handoff.

socket_path.description: Absolute remote-host agent socket. Registration lasts until this API connection closes.

TabCreateAgentParams.description:
Creates a tab running an interactive agent, typed into its new shell as
if the user had launched it there.

kind.description: A canonical agent id, as `agent.kind_list` returns.

TabCreateChildParams.description:

workspace, so it never shows as a top-level tab first. A separate method
from `tab.create`, whose shape is frozen: an older server rejects this one
instead of ignoring the parent and creating a top-level tab.

TodoAction.description: What the coordinator may answer an event with.

oneOf.description:
The worker's turn is accepted: stop it, verify, cherry-pick. The
approval is bound to the commit and base the event showed: a branch
that moved since is reviewed again instead of landed.

Start the next attempt, its task text being the review of this one
(at most 3 attempts): the next attempt's branch starts from this
attempt's commit, and its task is this attempt's with the review
appended. After `retry_conflict`: start that attempt from the base
instead, without the previous commit (no task text).
Answer the worker's pending question.

Run the verify again with the environment this resume sends (after
a check was `unavailable`).
SIGKILL the worker that is still alive after its stop.
Run the registered install again (after `install_failed`).
Go on without the install (after `install_failed`).
Edit and commit the TODO again (after `todo_failed`).
Go on without the TODO edit (after `todo_failed`).
Push again (after `push_failed`), still only as a fast-forward.

End the run as `aborted` where it stands, from any event it waits
on or from `blocked`: its worker is stopped when it still runs, and
its branches and commits (also one already on `master`) stay as
they are.

TodoResumeParams.description: The coordinator's answer to a run's event.

caller_pane_id.description:
The caller's pane. A run owned by another pane that is still there
is refused (`run_owned_elsewhere`); once the owner's pane or agent
is gone, the caller takes the run over: its pane, agent session and
workspace then own the run and its later workers.

close.description:
With `approve`: the decision that closes the item. The run removes
the item from `TODO.md` and adds the decision to `DECISIONS.md` as a
section (its first line, when it starts with `#`, is the section's
title; otherwise the item's title is), committed by path. Excludes
`note`.

decision.description: With `answer`: allow or deny for an approval.

env.description:
The caller's environment, sent again with every resume (`HERDR_*`
dropped) and kept in the server's memory only, never stored. A
resume without it leaves the server none: the run's next check is
then `unavailable`.

event.description:
The event answered: the `event_id` `todo.wait` returned. Any other
is refused as stale (`todo_event_stale`).

ignore_usage.description:
With `retry`: start the next attempt even while the usage gate
refuses, on the user's word; recorded in the run's events.

message.description: With `answer`: the message the model gets with a denial.

note.description:
With `approve`: lines the run appends to the item in `TODO.md` after
the install (`scripts/todo_edit.py append-to`), committed by path.

request_id.description:
With `answer`: the question answered; the only pending one when
absent.

task.description:
With `retry` (of a `review` or `verify_failed` event): the review of
the attempt, which the next attempt's task appends to this one's.
Refused after `retry_conflict`, which keeps the review.

TodoReviewParams.description: `todo.review`: one attempt of a run as the coordinator reviews it.

attempt.description: The attempt (1 for the first); the run's current one when absent.

diff.description: Also the full diff (`git diff base commit`), not only its stat.

TodoRunParams.description:
Drives one TODO item from preflight to a cherry-pick onto the
repository's `master` and on through the registered install, the TODO
update, a fast-forward push to `origin` and the cleanup of its merged
branches: a persisted, resumable run that starts a headless worker in the
repository's folder slot, turns what needs the coordinator (a question
outside the worker policy, the turn's end, a failed verify, install, TODO
edit or push) into run events, and verifies the worker's commit with a
registered check before picking it.

checks.description:
The names of checks in the repository's `.herdr/checks.toml`, run
in this order; every one must pass.

cwd.description: A directory in the repository (the CLI sends its working directory).

env.description:
The caller's environment, which the check runs with (`HERDR_*`
dropped); kept in the server's memory only, never stored.

ignore_usage.description:
Start even while the usage gate refuses (Claude's usage is high or
unknown), on the user's word; recorded in the run's events.

item.description:
The TODO item's id (`t-abcd2345`); it must be in the repository's
`TODO.md`.

message.description:
The exact commit subject the worker must use: a lowercase
conventional subject (`feat: ...`), one line.

owner_pane_id.description:
The coordinator's pane, which owns the run's workers (their
questions, obligations and coordination tenure) and resumes the run.

paths.description: Git glob pathspecs (`src/**`, `AGENTS.md`) the commit may touch.

task.description: The worker's task text, stored with the run as it is.

workspace_id.description: The coordinator's workspace, which lists the run's workers.

commit.description:
Only the run that landed this commit (a sha or a prefix of at least
7 characters, the landed commit or the worker's): found in the
store's landings, else by the `Herdr-Run` trailer of the commit in
`repo`'s history. Refused with `todo_run_not_found` when neither
names a run.

repo.description: Only the runs of this repository: a directory in it.

after.description:
The `event_id` the previous wait returned: only a later event
counts. A run that ended (`done`, `blocked`, `aborted`) returns its
last event however old.

refresh.description: Ask the server to start a refresh now; the response still returns cached values.

enabled.description: Whether the server polls providers at all.

provider.description: Provider id from `usage.settings`, such as `claude` or `openai_api`.

WorkerAckParams.description: The owner acknowledges having handled the worker's events up to `seq`.

seq.description:
The `seq` handled: the one `worker.wait` with `until: attention` or
`worker.obligations` returned. An ack at or below the acknowledged
one changes nothing; one past the worker's latest event is refused.

WorkerAnswerParams.description:
Answers a worker's pending question: a tool approval or an
`AskUserQuestion`. The worker waits for it without a time limit.

answers.description:
`AskUserQuestion` only: one answer per question, in order. Each is an
option's label, its 1-based number, or free text; a multi-select
question takes several labels or numbers separated by commas.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means
(`worker_command_conflict` when reused with other parameters). A
repeated id returns the stored outcome without doing it again: the
same reply, or the same refusal.

decision.description:
`allow` or `deny` for an approval. For an `AskUserQuestion`, `deny`
declines to answer and `allow` (or absent) sends `answers`.

message.description: The message the model gets with a denial.

request_id.description:
The question to answer. When absent, the only pending question; an
answer without it is refused while several are pending. A question
that is no longer pending is refused with `worker_question_gone`.

WorkerCommandTarget.description: A worker and the client's id for a command on it (`worker.stop`).

caller_pane_id.description:
The pane that sends the stop (the CLI sends its `HERDR_PANE_ID`).
When it is the worker's owner, the exit it causes is acknowledged
with it, so the owner owes nothing for an end it asked for.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means
(`worker_command_conflict` when reused with other parameters). A
repeated id returns the stored outcome without doing it again: the
same reply, or the same refusal.

oneOf.description:
Stop admitting new turns: `worker.prompt` and `worker.start` are

server hands off. Starting an active drain keeps it as it is.
Only report the drain and the workers in a turn.
Admit new turns again.

reason.description:

WorkerEscalateParams.description: The owner hands one of the worker's pending questions to the user.

request_id.description:
The question to escalate; one that is no longer pending is refused
with `worker_question_gone`.

WorkerGeneratedFile.description: A committed file and the shell command that regenerates it.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means
(`worker_command_conflict` when reused with other parameters). A
repeated id returns the stored outcome without doing it again: the
same reply, or the same refusal.

turn.description:
The turn to interrupt: its `turn_seq` (the `seq` of the user message
that began it, as `worker.prompt` returns it). Refused with
`worker_turn_ended` once that turn has ended, so a repeated interrupt
never reaches the next turn. When absent, whatever runs.

caller_pane_id.description:
The pane that sends the kill (the CLI sends its `HERDR_PANE_ID`).
When it is the worker's owner, the exit it causes is acknowledged
with it, so the owner owes nothing for an end it asked for.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means
(`worker_command_conflict` when reused with other parameters). A
repeated id returns the stored outcome without doing it again: the
same reply, or the same refusal.

force.description:
Needed to signal anything for a worker that is `exited` or `lost`:
without it such a kill is refused with `worker_needs_force`, and the

owner_pane_id.description: Only the workers this pane owns; every owned worker when absent.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means

text.description: The next user message; accepted only between turns.

WorkerRunsParams.description: Lists the workers' runs grouped by the TODO item they worked on.

item.description: Only the runs of this item (`t-abcd2345`); then no unassigned runs.

repo.description:
Only the runs in this repository: a directory in it, or the path
`repo` shows (the parent of its git common directory).

WorkerStartParams.description:
Starts a headless Claude worker: `claude -p` over stream-json pipes, no
terminal. The server owns the process; clients only ask about it.

base.description: With `folder_slot`: what the branch starts from; `master` when absent.

branch.description:
With `folder_slot`: the new branch checked out in the slot; it must
not exist yet.

command_id.description:
A client's id for this command, unique per command it means
(`worker_command_conflict` when reused with other parameters). A
repeated id returns the stored outcome without doing it again: the
same reply, or the same refusal.

cwd.description: Working directory; file tools are allowed only inside its real path.

folder_slot.description:
Runs the worker in the persistent git worktree
`<repository parent>/herdr-worktrees/<folder_slot>` of `cwd`'s
repository instead of in `cwd`, one worker at a time, so its build
caches stay warm. Needs `branch`.

fresh_build.description: With `folder_slot`: removes the slot's `target/` and Zig cache first.

item.description:
The TODO item the worker works on: its stable id `t-` and 8
lowercase base32 characters (`t-abcd2345`). `worker.runs` lists the

directory; a worker without one is listed as unassigned.

model.description: Passed to `claude --model`; the CLI's default when absent.

name.description:
The worker's task, as the sidebar names it; the prompt's first line
when absent.

owner_pane_id.description:
The pane of the coordinator that starts the worker (the CLI sends its
`HERDR_PANE_ID`): the worker's owner, whose `worker.obligations` list
the worker's events it has not acknowledged.

owner_session_id.description:
The owner's agent session (the CLI sends Claude Code's
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`), so the owner is the session, not only the
pane that holds it.

workspace_id.description: The space the worker belongs to, which the sidebar lists it under.

WorkerVerifyParams.description:
Herdr checks a worker's commit and decides its verdict, instead of the
worker's own word (`WORKER-DONE`). Runs in the worker's directory,
outside its sandbox, after the worker has ended.

allowed_paths.description:
Git glob pathspecs (`src/**`, `AGENTS.md`) the commit's changed
paths must stay within.

base.description: The commit the worker's branch started from.

command.description:
A shell command (`sh -c`) that must exit 0 in the worker's directory,
such as the tests of the change. It runs as long as it takes.

env.description:
The caller's environment, which `command` and the `generated`
commands run with instead of the server's (`HERDR_*` variables are
dropped). The CLI sends its own; absent, they run in the server's
environment.

expected_message.description: The exact commit message: one subject line, no body or trailers.

generated.description: Generated files that must regenerate to the committed bytes.

draining.description:
The `draining` the previous reply showed: the wait also returns when
a drain starts or ends (`worker.drain` `cancel`).

in_turn.description:
The workers the caller already knows are in a turn (the previous
reply's `in_turn`). The wait returns as soon as the workers in a turn
differ from these, or at once when none is in a turn.

after.description:
With `until: attention` only: the `seq` the previous attention reply
carried. A pending question asked or a turn ended at or before it does
not count again; only what later events bring does.

until.description: What to wait for; `turn_end` when absent.

oneOf.description: A finished, failed or interrupted turn, or the process's end.
The process's end (`exited` or `lost`).

The first of a pending question, a finished, failed or interrupted
turn, or the process's end; answered with `worker_attention`.

bookmarked.description:
True to bookmark the workspace, false to remove the bookmark;

Workspace whose focused pane supplies the `follow` cwd policy.

The tab whose pane created this worktree space with `herdr worktree

oneOf.description: The owner acknowledges the worker's events up to a `seq`.

`worker.take_over` that also retries a takeover an earlier server

Blocks until the run has an event after `after` that needs the

One attempt of a run as the coordinator reviews it: its task, the

The TODO items herdr recorded, each with its latest record.

awaiting_reply.description:
The agent's last turn ended by asking the user something (reported through
`pane.report_awaiting_reply`), nobody has typed into the pane since, and it is idle.

completion_seq.description: The current idle transition completed work, independently of who has viewed it.

limited.description: The limit the agent's last turn ended on (`pane.report_limit`), while it idles.

question.description:
What the agent asks while it waits on the user: the question it reported with
`pane.report_awaiting_reply`, or while blocked its hook's message.

task.description: What the agent reported it works on now (`pane.report_task`).

waiting_since_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds since when the agent waits on the user: blocked, awaiting a reply,
or stopped by a limit.

resets_at.description: Unix seconds when the limit resets, from herdr's usage report of the agent's provider.

AgentLimitKind.description: Which limit ended an agent's turn; the remedies differ.

oneOf.description: A usage or rate limit that resets on its own.
Out of credits or a billing problem: waiting does not help.

AgentPromptRequest.description: A prompt herdr typed into an agent and how far the turn it started got.

error.description: The error a `failed` turn ended on.

oneOf.description: Typed into the agent; the turn it starts has not been reported yet.
The agent reported that a turn started with this prompt.
That turn ended.
The agent does not report its turns, so herdr cannot follow this prompt.
That turn ended on an error the agent reported; see `error`.

The turn was interrupted: herdr sent an interrupt key while it worked, or the agent
reported its end as interrupted.
The agent's process ended before the turn did.

Another turn started before this one reported its end, with no signal saying why; also
any state this client does not know.

AgentTurnEndReason.description: How the turn of a followed prompt ended.

oneOf.description: The agent reported the turn's end (Claude's `Stop`).
The agent reported the turn ended on an error (Claude's `StopFailure`); see `error`.

The turn was interrupted: herdr sent the agent an interrupt key (Esc, Ctrl-C) while it
worked and another turn started before its end report, or the agent reported its end
as interrupted.
The agent's own process ended, or its pane closed, before the turn ended.

Herdr does not follow this request: it never did, it was dropped as the oldest, or the
server restarted and lost it. Its turn's outcome is not known.

Another turn started before this one reported its end, with no signal saying why: the
user may have interrupted it (Claude reports no `Stop` for a turn ended with Esc), or
the agent took a queued message into its work. Also any reason this client does not
know.

CoordinatorInfo.description:
One coordination tenure: who coordinated a repository's TODO, from when
to when. Its id is its own, never a pane's or an agent session's: those
are its bindings.

end_reason.description:
Why it ended: `ended` (`coordinator.end`), `role_cleared` (its tab's
role was cleared), `orphaned` (its pane closed or its agent exited,
also when found at server start), or the reason `coordinator.end`
was given.

epoch.description: Grows by one with each tenure of the repository.

item.description: The TODO item it works on; not recorded yet.

pane_id.description: Its latest binding's pane and agent session.

repo.description: The repository: the parent of its git common directory.

ahead.description: Commits not on the upstream yet; 0 without an upstream.

current.description: Checked out in the workspace's own checkout.

upstream_gone.description: The configured upstream branch no longer exists.

worktree_path.description: Another checkout (worktree) that has this branch checked out.

HistoryAttempt.description: One attempt of a run on the item, from the run's records.

commit.description: The attempt's commit as the coordinator's decision saw it.

landed_sha.description: The commit the attempt landed on `master`.

HistoryDeletedItem.description:
An item herdr saw in `TODO.md` (at a claim) that is gone from it without
a `closed` record.

last.description: Its latest record, when it has one.

HistoryEvent.description: One record of an item's life, in the order they were written.

id.description: The record's number, growing in the order of writing.

oneOf.description:
A run started on the item; `item_text` is its text in `TODO.md`
then.
The coordinator's note was appended to the item; `text` is the note.

The item left `TODO.md` for `DECISIONS.md`: `text` is the decision,
`item_text` the item's last text, `follow_ups` the items added since
the claim.
The run was aborted; `text` is why.
The run was blocked; `text` is why.

runs.description: The runs the records name, oldest first.

title.description:
The item's title, from its text at the last claim; for an item
whose records hold no text, from `TODO.md` while it is still there.

HistoryItemSummary.description: An item with its latest record.

title.description:
The item's title, from its text at the last claim; for an item
whose records hold no text, from `TODO.md` while it is still there.

HistoryOpenClaim.description:
A claim no `noted`, `closed`, `aborted` or `blocked` record of its run
followed.

run_status.description: The run's status now; absent when the store has no such run.

HistoryReconcile.description: What `history.reconcile` found; it reports, it never changes a record.

HistoryRun.description: A run on the item, with its attempts.

todo_commit.description: The run's TODO commit (its note or close), when it made one.

warnings.description:
Warnings collected at link time or on registry load (e.g. unknown event names,
missing manifest file). Non-fatal — the entry is kept and surfaced by plugin.list.

NotificationRecord.description:
A notification the server sent its clients, as `notification.list`
returns it: the server keeps the last 100 in memory, newest last, and
loses them on restart.

id.description: Increases with every notification of this server run.

kind.description:
`needs_attention`, `finished`, `update_installed` or `custom`; other
values may come later.

repeats.description:
How many notifications of this kind the pane sent in a row, this one
standing for all of them (a repeat replaces the older entry). Absent:
one.

request.description:
What the agent asked or said when it needed the user: its own message
from the hook report (an approval prompt or a question), one line.
Absent when the agent reported none.

task.description:
What the agent was working on when this fired: its terminal title,
cleaned and cut to one line. Absent when the pane had no meaningful
title (a bare shell or program name, a path).

unix_ms.description: When the server sent it, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

PaneLinkRegion.description: Inclusive display-cell columns on a pane's current viewport.

oneOf.description: Outer popup size in terminal cells, including the border.
Outer popup size as a percentage of the terminal area, for example 80%.

account.description:
Which login the allowance was read with, so data of the wrong account
is visible. Never a credential.

completion_tokens.description: Text-completion tokens over the same period as `spend`.

error_kind.description: Why the latest refresh failed; set together with `status: error`.

message.description: Error or hint for a status other than `ok`.

notes.description: Extra provider-specific facts for detail views.

observed_at.description: Unix seconds of the last successful observation.

provider.description: Stable provider id such as `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`, `deepseek`, or `openrouter`.

reset_credits.description:
Unredeemed one-time allowance resets, redeemed in the provider's own tool.
Clients hide credits whose `expires_at` has passed, since reports can be cached.

setup.description:
What the user must do before the provider can be read, one step per
line. Set together with `status: error`.

spend.description: Pay-as-you-go spend since `since`, one per currency. Not a prepaid balance.

oneOf.description: No observation has completed yet.
The latest refresh failed; windows and balances keep the last good values.
A future status this client does not understand.

system.description:
Absent where the platform has no fixed pool (Windows) or the
count cannot be read.

oneOf.description:
`worker.wait`'s reply with `until: attention`: why it returned, the
questions pending then, the worker, and `seq`, its latest event's,
which the next wait passes as `after`.

`worker.obligations`' reply: the owned workers with an event their
owner has not acknowledged, oldest worker first.
`worker.drain`'s and `worker.wait_drained`'s reply.

`worker.runs`' reply: each item's runs, the item whose first run
started first first, then the runs started without an item.
`worker.verify`'s reply: the verdict herdr decided and its evidence.
`todo.run`'s, `todo.resume`'s and `todo.status`' reply.
`todo.runs`' reply, oldest first.

landing.description: With `commit`: the landing that named the run.

oneOf.description: `todo.review`'s reply: one attempt of a run in one view.

`history.list`'s reply: each recorded item with its latest record,
the most recent first.
`history.item`'s reply.
`history.reconcile`'s reply.
`todo.wait`'s reply: the event and the run as it is now.
`coordinator.start`'s and `coordinator.end`'s reply.
`coordinator.status`'s reply: the active tenures, oldest first.
`worker.kill`'s reply: the worker and what was signalled.

Canonical ids of the interactive agents whose executable is on the
server's `PATH`, in Herdr's agent order.
`agent.wait_turn`: how the followed prompt's turn ended.

error.description: The error a `failed` turn ended on.

pane_id.description: The pane the request was typed into, when herdr still knew the request.

oneOf.description:
Acknowledgement for the client-shell surface interest lease. This method is new on the
endpoint protocol, so its revision-bearing result can establish an activation floor.

endpoint_protocol_generation.description: Stable client-owned endpoint generation supported by this server.

health_check.description: Whether this server supports endpoint health probes.

ssh_agent_registration.description: Supports connection-scoped `server.ssh_agent.register` on the local JSON API.

surface_interest.description: Whether this server supports explicit client-shell surface interest.

SystemPtyUsageInfo.description: System-wide pseudo-terminal usage, sampled at most once a second.

in_use.description: Pseudo-terminals open on the whole system, not only Herdr's panes.

max.description: The kernel limit (`kern.tty.ptmx_max` on macOS, `kernel.pty.max` on Linux).

required_free.description:
Free pseudo-terminals a new pane must leave; below this Herdr refuses
the spawn with `pty_exhausted`.

TabActivity.description: What a running tab's job is doing, as far as its runner can tell.

oneOf.description: No output for a while and (almost) no CPU: the job runs but does nothing.
A value from a newer server that this build does not know.

activity.description: What the running job does (see `tab.set_status`); absent when unknown.

bookmarked.description:
Whether the user bookmarked the tab (see `tab.bookmark`). Absent
means false.

role.description:
What the tab's agent does for the user (see `tab.set_role`); absent
when none was set.

TabJobMetadata.description: Runtime facts supplied by a job runner; presentation belongs to clients.

TabRole.description:
What the agent in a tab does for the user, as whoever opened the tab says
(never derived from the agent's name or title).

oneOf.description:
Works through a list (a repository's TODO) by handing each item to a
worker.
Does one item, usually in a worktree of its own.
A value from a newer server that this build does not know.

TabStatus.description:
Outcome of the work a tab runs, set by whoever runs it (e.g. a job runner).
Clients choose how to show it and summarise a parent's children with it.

oneOf.description: A value from a newer server that this build does not know.

TodoAction.description: What the coordinator may answer an event with.

oneOf.description:
The worker's turn is accepted: stop it, verify, cherry-pick. The
approval is bound to the commit and base the event showed: a branch
that moved since is reviewed again instead of landed.

Start the next attempt, its task text being the review of this one
(at most 3 attempts): the next attempt's branch starts from this
attempt's commit, and its task is this attempt's with the review
appended. After `retry_conflict`: start that attempt from the base
instead, without the previous commit (no task text).
Answer the worker's pending question.

Run the verify again with the environment this resume sends (after
a check was `unavailable`).
SIGKILL the worker that is still alive after its stop.
Run the registered install again (after `install_failed`).
Go on without the install (after `install_failed`).
Edit and commit the TODO again (after `todo_failed`).
Go on without the TODO edit (after `todo_failed`).
Push again (after `push_failed`), still only as a fast-forward.

End the run as `aborted` where it stands, from any event it waits
on or from `blocked`: its worker is stopped when it still runs, and
its branches and commits (also one already on `master`) stay as
they are.

TodoApproval.description: The `(commit, base)` an approval is bound to.

TodoEventKind.description: A run's event that needs the coordinator or ends the run.

oneOf.description: The worker asked a question the worker policy does not decide.

The worker's turn ended (or the worker did): review its work. Also
raised before the cherry-pick when the branch's tip is not the
commit the approval named (`error` says so): review it again.

The verify failed or could not run: give the next attempt's task,
or verify again.

Raised by `todo.status` while the worker has not exited since its
stop (it ignores SIGTERM): force-stop it. The run goes on by itself
when the worker exits first.

The registered install failed or could not run: retry it, skip it
or abort.
The TODO edit or its commit failed: retry it, skip it or abort.

`master` could not be pushed as a fast-forward (or the push failed):
retry it or abort. Never forced.
The run is blocked; it takes `abort`.
The run was aborted: why, its branches and its commits.

The previous attempt's commit does not cherry-pick onto the next
attempt's branch (`error` names the conflict): retry starts that
attempt from the base without it, or abort.

TodoLanding.description:
A commit a run landed on `master`, with the run and attempt it came
from.

landed_sha.description: The commit on `master`, which carries the trailers.

ts_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the landing; absent when found by trailers.

worker_commit.description: The worker's commit it was picked from (subject only).

worker_id.description:
The attempt's worker, whose journal is the run's transcript; absent
when the store does not know the attempt.

oneOf.description: The worker store's record, written when the run landed the commit.

The commit's `Herdr-Item` and `Herdr-Run` trailers (the store has no
record of it: another machine's run, or a sha the upstream rebase
changed).

TodoReview.description:
One attempt of a run in one view: the run's `attempts` row, the
worker's journal (its transcript) and `git diff base commit` in the
run's repository. Nothing of it is stored apart from those.

approved.description: With `approve`: the commit and base the approval is bound to.

attempts.description: How many attempts the run has had so far.

base.description: The commit the attempt is verified and reviewed against.

commit.description:
The attempt's commit: the one the coordinator's decision saw, else
the verify's head, else the branch's tip when it is past the base.

decision.description:
The coordinator's decision on the attempt: `approve`, `retry` or
`abort`.

diff.description: `git diff base commit`, when asked for (`diff`).

diff_error.description: Why the diff could not be read (no commit yet, git failed).

final_message.description: The worker's last reply (its last turn's result).

from_attempt.description: The previous attempt and its commit this one's branch starts from.

landed_sha.description: The commit on `master` the attempt landed as.

questions.description: The questions the worker asked, oldest first, each with its answer.

review_text.description: With `retry`: the review the next attempt got.

task.description:
The task the worker got: its first prompt, the run's contract
appended; the run's stored task when its journal is not there.

tool_failures.description: The tool calls that failed or were denied, oldest first.

verification.description:
Herdr's latest verify of the attempt: each check with its outcome
and evidence.

TodoReviewQuestion.description: A question the worker asked and how it was answered.

answer.description:
The answer (`allow`, `deny` or the choices); absent while it waits
or when it was never answered.

TodoReviewToolFailure.description: A tool call that failed or was denied.

detail.description: The error, or who denied it and why.

input.description: The call's most telling input: the command, the path or the URL.

actions.description: What `todo.resume` takes for it; empty once the run ended.

commits.description: The commits since the base, oldest first.

diff_stat.description: The branch's changes since the base (`git diff --stat`).

error.description:
With `blocked` and `aborted`: why (`aborted` also names the run's
branches); with `still_alive`: what is still running; with a
`review` raised before the cherry-pick: the approved commit and the
branch's tip; with `retry_conflict`: the commit and the conflict;
with `install_failed`, `todo_failed` and `push_failed`: what failed,
with the output's last lines.

verification.description: With `verify_failed`: the verdict and each check's evidence.

attempt.description: 1 for the first worker; each retry adds one, at most 3.

base.description:
`master`'s commit when the run started, which each attempt's branch
starts from.

checks.description: The registered checks the verify runs, in order.

error.description: Why it is blocked or was aborted.

installed_build.description:
The build the install reported (the registered `build_id` command's
first line), or `installed` when none is registered.

kept_branches.description:
Merged branches of the run the cleanup kept because a worktree has
them checked out (the folder slot); a later run's cleanup deletes
them once the slot moved on.

last_acked_seq.description: The highest worker event the run has handled (acknowledged).

picked.description:
The commit the cherry-pick made on `master`, with the `Herdr-Item`
and `Herdr-Run` trailers.

pushed.description: The `master` commit `origin` has after the push.

task.description:
The current attempt's task text: the first attempt's is the run's,
each later one is the previous attempt's with its review appended.

todo_commit.description: The commit of the TODO update on `master`.

oneOf.description: The driver works on its step.
It waits for the coordinator's `todo.resume` to its pending event.

It stopped and needs a person: a refused preflight, a conflict, the
attempts used up. Nothing more happens unless the coordinator
aborts it.

The commit is on `master`, installed, recorded and pushed (each as
far as registered and approved), and the merged branches are gone.

The coordinator aborted it; its worker exited, its branches and
commits are left as they were.
Stops the attempt's worker before the next attempt starts.
Runs the repository's registered install command.

Appends the coordinator's note to the item, or closes it into
`DECISIONS.md`, and commits that by path.
Pushes `master` to `origin`, only as a fast-forward.
Deletes the run's branches that are fully merged.

The coordinator aborted the run: its worker is stopped, then the
run ends `aborted`.
The tool ran and returned an error.

The policy, a pre-tool check, the user or the CLI's permission
mode denied the call.

UsageAccount.description:
The login a provider's allowance was read with: where herdr found it and
whom it names, never the credential itself.

config_dir.description:
The provider CLI's config directory that selects the login, such as
`~/.claude` or `$CODEX_HOME`.

email.description: Account email, where the provider's data names one.

organization.description: Organization name, where the provider's data names one.

source.description:
Where the login came from: `file:<path>`, `keychain:<item name>`,
`env:<variable>`, or `cli:<command>` when the provider's own CLI reads
its login.

total.description: Decimal amount as reported by the provider.

cached_input.description: The part of `input` served from the prompt cache.

since.description: Unix seconds where the reported period starts.

oneOf.description: The provider rate-limited the usage endpoint; herdr backs off.
The login or key was missing, expired or rejected.
Something must be set up first; `setup` on the provider lists the steps.
The request did not reach the provider.
Any other failure: an unexpected response or a provider CLI error.
A future kind this client does not understand.

Observed by the latest refresh, recently enough, and the window has
not reset since.

Older than two refresh intervals, or the window reset after it was
observed.
The latest refresh failed; `error_kind` says why.
A future state this client does not understand; treat as unknown.

credential.description:
`not_required`, `found`, `missing` or `unsafe`; clients treat other
values as unknown.

warning.description: Why turning it on needs care, such as an organization-wide key.

UsageReport.description: Latest subscription/API allowance observed for each configured provider.

enabled.description: False when usage polling is disabled in the server config.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds when the unused credit expires.

kind.description: Provider's kind of reset, such as `codexRateLimits`.

title.description: Provider's title, such as `Full reset (Weekly + 5 hr)`.

UsageSettings.description: The server's own `[usage]` choices and whether each provider can run.

limit.description: Spend limit for the same period and currency, as set at the provider.

limit_enforcing.description: The provider is rejecting requests because the limit was reached.

since.description: Unix seconds where the reported period starts.

error_kind.description: Why the latest refresh failed, with `freshness: failed`.

freshness.description:
Whether `used_percent` is current. Only `fresh` is; a `stale` or
`failed` window's `used_percent` is the last observation, and the
current value is unknown (neither 0 nor 100). Absent from older servers.

id.description: Stable window id such as `five_hour` or `weekly`.

resets_at.description: Unix seconds when the window resets.

used_percent.description: Consumed share of the window allowance, 0-100.

oneOf.description: A question waits for an answer.
The turn finished, failed or was interrupted.
The process ended (`exited` or `lost`); nothing more will happen.
A reason this client does not know.
It could not run.
Not run: an earlier check made it meaningless (a dirty worktree).

WorkerDrain.description: The server's drain and the workers it waits for.

ended.description:
`worker.wait_drained` only: the workers of its `in_turn` that are no
longer in a turn, as they are now.

in_turn.description:
The running workers in a turn: their first turn or a prompted one
has not ended.

started_ms.description: When the drain started, Unix milliseconds.

starting.description: Worker starts admitted before the drain and not registered yet.

degraded.description:
Why the worker's record is incomplete: writing one of its events to
the worker store or its journal failed, with the error. The status
still follows the worker; a restart may not show what was lost.

end_note.description:
How a worker ended that keeps its last turn's state: one that had
finished its turn when its server ended shows that turn's state with
"ended by a server restart", not `lost`.

item.description: The TODO item given at start (`worker.start`'s `item`).

journal_path.description:
The JSONL journal of every event in and out, exported after each
event is stored; `herdr worker log` reads it.

name.description:
The worker's task: the `name` given at start, else the prompt's
first line.

owner_coordinator_id.description:
The coordination tenure (`c-...`, see `coordinator.start`) its owner
pane was bound to when it started; absent when it had none.

owner_pane_id.description:
The pane that started the worker, its owner (`worker.start`'s
`owner_pane_id`).

pid.description: The CLI's process id, which also leads the worker's process group.

questions.description:
Questions the worker waits on, oldest first: `pending` ones and
those whose answer is being sent (`answering`); its state is
`waiting_approval` while there are any.

rate_limit.description: `rate_limit_info` of the last `rate_limit_event`, as the CLI sent it.

repo.description:
The repository of the worker's directory: the parent of its git
common directory, so every worktree of one repository has the same.

seq.description: The `seq` of the worker's latest event.

settled_questions.description:
The most recently settled questions, oldest first, with how each
ended.

stop_requested_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds when `worker.stop` sent SIGTERM, while the process
has not exited yet.

survives_handoff.description:
The worker runs and a live handoff keeps it running: a broker owns
its pipes, so the new server takes it over mid-turn. Absent for one
whose pipes the server owns (started by an older build, or on
Windows), which a handoff would end.

takeover_error.description:
Why the last takeover failed; its claim was released, so it can be
tried again.

takeover_id.description:
The takeover's unique id: its tab carries it in `HERDR_TAKEOVER_ID`
and its title.

takeover_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds when a takeover began (`worker.take_over`): the
worker is being ended so its session can resume in a tab.

takeover_tab_id.description: The tab the takeover opened to resume the worker's session.

takeover_unfinished.description:
A takeover claimed by an earlier server that did not record opening
its tab, and whose tab (by its id) or a process resuming the session
was not found: a tab may or may not resume the session. Only
`worker.force_take_over` retries it.

tool_sessions.description:
Sessions of the worker's tool processes seen so far (Claude Code runs
each Bash tool with `setsid`); `worker.kill` ends those whose leader
is still the process recorded with it.

turn_seq.description:
The `seq` of the user message that began the current or last turn;
`worker.interrupt` takes it as `turn`. In `worker.prompt`'s reply it
is the message that prompt appended; in `worker.interrupt`'s, the
turn it interrupted.

WorkerItemRuns.description:
One item's runs, oldest first. Ids of different repositories are never
grouped together.

repo.description:
The repository the item's id belongs to; absent when the workers'
directory was not in a git repository.

title.description:
The item's title: its first line in the repository's `TODO.md`,
without the box and the id, cut to 80 characters; absent when the
file has no item with that id (a finished item leaves it).

WorkerKillReport.description: What `worker.kill` did with the worker's recorded tool sessions.

pids.description:
Processes sent SIGKILL: the members of each recorded session whose
leader still is the process recorded with it (same start time) that
did not start before that leader.

stale_sessions.description:
Sessions whose leader is gone or is now another process with the
same pid: skipped.

unverified_sessions.description:
Sessions recorded without their leader's start time (journals from
before herdr recorded it): not verified, not killed.

WorkerObligation.description: A worker whose owner has an event of it to handle.

questions.description:
With `question`: the pending questions asked after the acknowledged
`seq`.

reason.description:
What it needs: `question` (an unanswered question asked after the
acknowledged `seq`), `turn_end` (a turn ended after it, to review) or
`gone` (the worker exited or was lost after it).

seq.description:
The worker's latest event's `seq`; `worker.ack` with it settles
everything listed here.

WorkerQuestion.description:
A question a worker waits on: a `can_use_tool` request the policy left to
the user.

escalated.description:
Why the question was handed to the user, for a worker with an owner:
the owner escalated it, its pane closed, its agent exited, hit a
limit, ended its turn or is blocked on its own question, or herdr
restarted without it. Until then the user's `?` list shows it quietly
as awaiting the coordinator. A worker without an owner asks the user
at once and never sets it.

reason.description: Why the policy did not decide it.

request_id.description: The CLI's control request id; `worker.answer` names it.

since_ms.description: Unix milliseconds since when the worker waits.

state.description:
Where its answer is: `pending` (only such a question is answered),
or `answering`.

text.description:
One line for the user: the Bash command, the question, or the tool's
input.

oneOf.description: A tool the policy does not decide; answered with allow or deny.
An `AskUserQuestion`; answered with the chosen options.
A kind this client does not know.

WorkerQuestionState.description:
Where a question's answer is. `answered` means the answer was written to
the worker's input; the CLI sends no acknowledgement of it, and herdr
does not track which client was shown the question, so neither
"acknowledged" nor "delivered" is a state of its own.

oneOf.description: Waits for an answer.

An answer is stored and being written to the worker; a failed write
makes it `pending` again.
The answer was written to the worker's input.
The CLI withdrew the question.

Ended unanswered: its turn ended, the worker exited or was lost, or
a server restart found its answer not confirmed written.
A state this client does not know.

WorkerRun.description:
One run: one worker process from its start to its end. A worker sent
back with `worker.prompt` adds turns to the same run.

commits.description:
The commit shas its turns' results named on `WORKER-DONE <sha>`
lines, in order.

ended_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of its exit or loss; absent while it runs.

started_ms.description: Unix milliseconds of the worker's start.

verification.description: The latest `worker.verify` of its work; absent when none ran.

oneOf.description: Its process still runs.
It ended after a turn that finished.
Its last turn failed.
It exited otherwise: stopped, interrupted, or before a turn ended.
Its server ended while it ran.
Its record is incomplete (a store or journal write failed).

WorkerSettledQuestion.description: A question that is no longer open.

how.description: What ended it, as `worker_question_gone` says it.

oneOf.description: Spawned; no `system/init` yet.
A turn is running.

The CLI asked for a tool permission or a question that is not
answered yet; `questions` lists those left to the user.
The last turn ended with `result/success`.

The last turn ended with an error `result` other than an interrupt,
or with a model refusal (`last_result.failure` says which).
The last turn was interrupted (`terminal_reason` `aborted_*`).
The process ended; `exit_code` or `exit_signal` says how.

The server that ran it ended before it did, during a turn; its
process is not ours any more. One between turns keeps its last
turn's state with `end_note` instead.
A state this client does not know.

WorkerTurnResult.description: The `result` message that ended the last turn.

failure.description:
Why herdr counts the turn as failed even when its `result` reads as
success: a model refusal in the turn, or a non-zero exit code right
after a finished turn.

permission_denials.description:
The `result`'s `permission_denials`: the tool uses denied in the
turn, as the CLI sent them.

text.description: The reply text, when the CLI sent one.

WorkerVerification.description: What `worker.verify` decided, with the evidence of each check.

commits.description: The commits from `base` to the head, oldest first.

head.description:
The branch's head when it was checked; absent when git could not
read it.

verified_ms.description: Unix milliseconds when the verdict was reached.

WorkerVerifyCheck.description:
One check: `commits`, `message`, `paths`, `clean_tree`, `processes`,
`generated` (with its `path`) or `command` (with its `name` when it is a
registered check of `todo.run`).

detail.description: The evidence: what failed, or the output's last lines.

name.description: With `command` of a `todo.run`: the registered check's name.

creator_tab_id.description:
The tab whose pane created this worktree space with `herdr worktree
create`. It is never reassigned, and the tab may have closed since.
